item.title: CBO says Iran war diving up inflation, puts price tag at $38 billion
item.description: Two new, independent reports show detailed looks at the costs of the war in Iran. It's led to shortages in U.S. weapons, supply chain bottlenecks, and a price tag in the tens of billions of dollars.

item.title: Family income rose and poverty fell in 2025 — but safety net cuts could erase gains
item.description: An annual report from the Census Bureau shows the average family made more money in 2025 than the year before, while the official poverty rate declined. Health care coverage was little changed from 2024.

item.title: What the 10-year Treasury yield hitting 5% means for inflation and the Fed
item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Stacey Vanek Smith, reporter for Bloomberg Businessweek, about the 10-year Treasury yield's brief rise to 5% Monday and how the Federal Reserve might react.

item.title: The powerful millionaires hiding in plain sight
item.description: They own car dealerships, law firms, dental practices, and restaurant chains. Collectively, these overlooked business owners hold far more wealth than the Forbes 400 — and wield considerable political power.

item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel asks KPMG chief economist Diane Swonk about the pressure the ongoing conflict in the Gulf is putting on the global economy.

item.title: Federal Reserve chairs historically over-communicate what's next. Kevin Warsh wants to say less
item.description: Fed chairs wield great power and they take great care to signal what they intend to do ahead of time to avoid surprises. Not Kevin Warsh though. He wants to say less, and investors are worried.

item.title: Cost of living has gone up 3.4% in the last year
item.description: A new report shows the cost of living in August was up 3.4% from a year ago. Investors think stubborn inflation makes it more likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.
